title: Mean Absolute Scaled Error (MASE)
summary: The average absolute gap between price and its own EMA, divided by a naive-forecast scale, over a rolling window of bars.
descriptionHtml:
Mean Absolute Scaled Error scores an exponential moving average as a forecast of price, divided by a scale meant to come from a naive forecast. The average is taken over Period bars and seeded with the simple average of its first Period values. On every bar the study takes the absolute gap between the source and the average and divides it by the scale.

The scale is measured once, on the first bar of the chart, as the mean absolute one-bar change of the source over the window. On the first bar there is no earlier bar to compare with, so no change is counted and the scale is set to 1 for the whole chart. In practice the reading therefore equals the plain mean absolute error, in price units.

The scaled errors are averaged over the last Period bars, at most 4000, counting only the bars that carry an error. The error is plotted as a shaded area in its own pane, and the reference average is drawn on the price chart.
howToReadHtml:
Read the value as the typical distance between price and its average over the recent past. A rising reading means price is pulling away from its average faster than before, which is common in a strong trend or a volatile stretch. A falling reading means price has settled near its average.

Because the scale settles at 1, the reading is in price units and grows with the price level, so compare it with its own history rather than with another instrument.

settings.label: Source
settings.html: The price series measured against its own average. The close by default.

settings.label: Period
settings.html: The length of the reference EMA and of the error averaging window, which is held to at most 4000 bars.

faq.q: Why does it read the same as MAE?
faq.html: The scale is measured only on the first bar, where no earlier bar exists to compare against, so it settles at 1 and the division leaves the error unchanged. The study keeps that calculation exactly as written.

faq.q: What is the EMA on the price chart?
faq.html: It is the forecast being scored. The pane shows how far price has been from that line on average.

faq.q: Why does the line start late?
faq.html: The EMA has no value until the chart has Period bars, so the error cannot be measured before then.

related.title: Median Absolute Error
related.summary: The rolling median of the absolute gap between an actual series and a predicted one, a typical error that ignores outliers.

related.title: Mean Absolute %Error (MAPE)
related.summary: The average absolute gap between price and its own EMA, as a percentage of price, over a rolling window of bars.

related.title: Median Absolute Percentage Error
related.summary: The rolling median of the percentage gap between an actual series and a predicted one, a forecast error score that one outlier bar barely moves.
